claims.text: Adding approximately 2–3 mol% Hf to ZrB2 and consolidating it by SPS at about 1750 °C will produce a refined, Hf-stabilized grain-boundary structure.
The proposed Hf-modified material will have greater strength than undoped, lower-temperature-processed ZrB2.
The proposed Hf-modified material will have greater oxidation resistance than undoped ZrB2.
The proposed Hf-modified material will have greater liquid plating-metal corrosion durability than undoped ZrB2.
Hf is chemically and crystallographically compatible with ZrB2.
Hf diffuses into ZrB2 grain boundaries during SPS at approximately 1750 °C.
Hf promotes diffusion bonding of ZrB2 at reduced sintering temperatures.
Hf addition during SPS yields a more uniform and refined ZrB2 grain structure.
Hf-enriched grain boundaries impede oxygen ingress.
Hf-enriched grain boundaries impede liquid-metal ingress.
Hf-doped ZrB2 processed by SPS at approximately 1750 °C will match or exceed the mechanical strength of ZrB2 processed above 2300 °C.
Hf-doped ZrB2 will significantly outperform both high-temperature-processed and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2 in oxidation resistance.
Hf-doped ZrB2 will significantly outperform both high-temperature-processed and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2 in liquid plating-metal corrosion resistance.
The proposed performance is expected to persist in oxygen-rich service conditions up to approximately 2000 °C.
The proposed performance is expected during prolonged exposure to liquid plating metals.
Undoped lower-temperature-produced ZrB2 specimens have inadequate oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Processing routes, Hf concentrations far outside 2–3 mol%, and service temperatures above approximately 2000 °C may not provide the proposed effect.
